executiveSummary: Relay drafts the first reply to every support ticket in the team's own voice. B2B customers wait a median of twelve hours for a first reply, and three topics fill most queues. In a 42-team beta, Relay cut first replies to 47 seconds and raised CSAT eleven points. It starts free, costs $29 per agent per month, and sets up in twenty minutes.

slides.slideTitle: Relay answers every customer in under a minute
slides.subtitle: Launch event · October 2026
slides.visualDescription: A dark stage, a single glowing inbox counter rolling down to zero
slides.speakerNotes:
- Welcome, and thanks for joining us live.
- Today we're launching Relay.
- In the next twenty minutes you'll see it answer real tickets, live, and you'll leave with a free account.
slides.intent: Make the audience expect something new

slides.slideTitle: What if your team never wrote a first reply again?
slides.speakerNotes:
- Think about your support team's morning.
- Most of it is typing answers they've typed a hundred times.
- What if that part simply disappeared?
slides.purpose: Poses the question the launch answers
slides.intent: Make the audience imagine the outcome

slides.slideTitle: Customers wait twelve hours for a first reply
keyBullets: 12 hours
median first reply time for B2B support teams in 2026
slides.speakerNotes:
- The median B2B team takes twelve hours to send a first reply.
- Customers expect one within the hour.
- Every hour of waiting shows up later as churn.
slides.purpose: Quantifies the gap between expectation and reality
slides.intent: Make the audience feel the cost of slow replies
slides.supportingFacts: Relay benchmark of 1,140 B2B support teams, Q2 2026

slides.slideTitle: Three questions make up most of every support queue
slides.subtitle: Share of tickets by topic, 1,140 teams
keyBullets: Order status, login, and billing are 62% of all tickets
slides.speakerNotes:
- We looked at 4.2 million tickets across 1,140 teams.
- Three topics dominate: order status, login, and billing.
- These are answerable from data you already have.
slides.purpose: Shows the repetitive nature of the work
slides.intent: Make the audience see the opportunity

slides.slideTitle: Macros and chatbots each solve only half the problem
keyBullets: Macros: fast, but agents still read, pick, and edit every one
Chatbots: deflect tickets, but customers hate being trapped in them
slides.speakerNotes:
- Teams have tried two things.
- Macros save typing but not thinking.
- Chatbots save agents but annoy customers.
- Neither gives you a great human reply, fast.
slides.purpose: Explains why existing tools fall short
slides.intent: Make the audience want a better option

slides.slideTitle: Agents spend their mornings retyping the same answers
keyBullets: I spend my mornings typing the same eleven answers. By lunch I've forgotten why I liked this job.
Support agent, Relay survey of 1,200 agents
slides.speakerNotes: This came from our survey of 1,200 support agents. It's the line we pinned to the wall when we started building. Relay exists so nobody has to write that sentence again.
slides.purpose: Gives the problem a human voice
slides.intent: Make the audience empathize with their own agents

slides.slideTitle: Relay drafts the first reply to every ticket, in your voice
slides.speakerNotes:
- So here it is.
- Relay reads every new ticket and drafts the first reply before an agent opens it.
- It sounds like your team, because it learned from your team.
slides.purpose: Delivers the big reveal in one line
slides.intent: Make the audience feel the 'aha' moment

slides.slideTitle: Watch Relay clear 200 tickets with one agent in ten minutes
slides.subtitle: Live demo
slides.visualDescription: Screen recording of the Relay inbox: draft replies appear beside each ticket, an agent presses Tab to send, the counter drops
slides.speakerNotes:
- Let's switch to the live demo.
- This is a real queue from one of our beta customers, anonymized.
- Watch the drafts appear in the right-hand column.
- Our agent, Sam, reviews and sends with one key.
slides.intent: Make the audience believe it works on real tickets

slides.slideTitle: Relay reads, drafts, and learns from every ticket
keyBullets: Reads: each new ticket, the customer's history, and your help center
Drafts: a reply in your team's voice, with the order or account already looked up
Learns: every edit an agent makes improves the next draft
slides.speakerNotes:
- Three things happen for every ticket.
- Relay reads context, not just the message.
- It looks up the order or account so the reply has real details.
- And it learns from every edit your agents make.
slides.intent: Make the audience trust the mechanism

slides.slideTitle: Beta teams answered faster and kept customers happier
slides.subtitle: 42 beta teams, June–September 2026
keyBullets: 47 sec: median first reply, down from 9 hours
68%: of drafts sent with no edits
+11 pts: CSAT across all 42 teams
3.2×: tickets handled per agent per hour
slides.speakerNotes:
- Forty-two teams used Relay for three months.
- Median first reply dropped from nine hours to 47 seconds.
- Two-thirds of drafts went out unedited.
- And CSAT went up eleven points, which surprised even us.
slides.purpose: Proves the product's impact with numbers
slides.intent: Make the audience believe the results

slides.slideTitle: Support leads say Relay sounds like their best day
keyBullets: Our queue used to be a Monday problem. Now it's empty by ten. — Aisha Bello, Head of Support, Kettle & Co.
Relay sounds like us on our best day. — Tom Brandt, CX Lead, Parcelpoint
slides.speakerNotes: Aisha's team of six handles 3,000 tickets a week. Tom's team was the most skeptical in the beta; they now auto-send order-status replies.

slides.slideTitle: Questions every support lead asks us first
keyBullets: Does Relay send anything on its own?: Never by default; you choose which topics can auto-send
Where does our data go?: It stays in your region and never trains shared models
How long does setup take?: About 20 minutes with Zendesk, Intercom, or Front
slides.speakerNotes:
- These three come up in every call.
- Nothing auto-sends unless you turn it on, topic by topic.
- Your data never trains anyone else's model.
- Setup is twenty minutes; we'll do it with you.
slides.intent: Make the audience feel safe to try it
